candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication administration and client education
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — insulin administration
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize the expected appearance and resuspension technique for NPH insulin before administration.

options.A: This is the expected appearance of the NPH insulin suspension after proper resuspension
options.B: The insulin should be completely clear after mixing and must be warmed if cloudiness remains
options.C: Any uniformly white appearance proves contamination and requires automatic disposal
options.D: NPH insulin is a clear long-acting solution that should never require resuspension

candidate.rationale: HUMULIN N (NPH/isophane insulin) is a suspension. Its DailyMed instructions direct gentle rolling and inversion before use and state that it should look white and cloudy after mixing. A clear appearance, lumps, or particles are reasons not to use the product. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: HUMULIN N should be gently rolled and inverted to mix and should appear white and cloudy after mixing; do not use if clear or if lumps/particles are present.
candidate.source_document_title: HUMULIN N — insulin human injection, suspension
candidate.source_locator: Patient Instructions for Use — Preparing your HUMULIN N dose, Steps 1-2; Pen preparation Steps 2-4
candidate.source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine (official FDA drug labeling)
candidate.stem: A nurse gently rolls and inverts a vial of NPH insulin before administration. After mixing, the insulin appears uniformly white and cloudy. How should the nurse interpret this finding?
